text:
Alice: heads up — noticed a bunch of 301/302 breakages from the gateway this morning when clients follow redirects. seems related to header rewrites (Host lost) and query dedupe.
Ben: repro steps?
Alice: curl -v 'https://api.redwood.dev/v1/items?foo=1&foo=1' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' -> server returns 301 to https://internal.svc/v1/items (Host becomes internal.svc) => signed client fails.
Carlos: that sounds like we are both normalizing query and rewriting host before we attach the original-host header. order matters.
Diana: do we even preserve Host by default for proxied upstreams? I thought we set upstream_host: true for internal services.
Ben: quick config snippet from the gateway that might be the culprit:
```
route {
  match: "/v1/*"
  strip_prefix: true
  normalize_query: true
  dedupe_query: true
  header_set: { "Host": "internal.svc" }
  header_remove: ["Cookie"]
}
```
Alice: yep that's essentially it. Setting Host early causes signed URLs and HMACs to fail when upstream redirects. clients expect Host to remain original.
Carlos: proposal: 1) run path normalization and query rewrites first (dedupe/sort) 2) apply header removals/injections that are safe 3) preserve X-Original-Host and only set Host on the wire if necessary for wire-level SNI, but keep orig for signatures.
Diana: +1 but edge case: some backends legitimately require Host matching to select vhost. we can't break that either.
Ben: maybe an explicit flag per route: preserve_original_host: true/false. default true for public-facing routes, false for internal-only.
Alice: also need a rule for cookies: remove cookies for cacheable endpoints, but not for auth routes. we should support conditional header_remove with matchers.
Carlos: something like:
```
header_rules:
  - if: { path_prefix: "/static/", method: GET }
    remove: ["Cookie", "Authorization"]
  - if: { header_exists: "X-Signed-Request" }
    preserve: ["Host", "Authorization"]
```
Diana: that looks good. Also telemetry: add counters for rewrite_actions and list of dropped headers per route so we can debug when clients break.
Alice: yes please. right now it's a black box. I want metrics: rewrite.host_preserve_skips, rewrite.header_drop_{name}, rewrite.query_dedupe_count.
infra-bot: telemetry metric created: gateway.rewrite_actions (tag: route, action)
Ben: ok, two implementation questions: 1) should path canonicalization run before query normalize? 2) how do we ensure redirects keep original Host when gateway follows the redirect vs passes raw redirect to client?
Carlos: for (1) canonicalize path (trailing slash, dot segments) first — query ordering doesn't affect path, but may affect cache keys. For (2) if gateway is configured to follow redirects (proxy_follow_redirects), preserve original host header when following and include X-Original-Host on the upstream request. If returning redirect to client, leave Location header untouched (don't rewrite host) unless explicit rewrite_location: true.
Diana: important: some clients expect deduped query ordering to remain stable, but we shouldn't change client-visible Location headers. Only rewrite Location when route.option.rewrite_location == true.
Alice: TL;DR: defaults: preserve client-visible headers/Location; do internal normalization (path/query) for routing/cache but keep original values in proxied responses unless explicitly overridden.
Ben: I'll draft a spec and add unit tests + harnessed curl tests. @Diana can you add the telemetry counters you mentioned?
Diana: on it. I'll add a short eval with replayed traffic to catch regressions.
Carlos: one more: add a feature flag for strict-compat-mode for customers that rely on exact Host/signature behavior.
Alice: nice. can we also add a short debug endpoint that returns "gateway.rewrite_log" for a request (list of rewrite steps) so engineers can repro without digging logs?
infra-bot: feature request created: GATEWAY-9483 — rewrite log endpoint + rewrite telemetry. assignee: Ben.
Ben: thanks. I'll push a PR with the config model and tests later today. ping me if you have specific failing curl outputs.
Alice: posted a sample failing curl output in case it's useful:
```
* Connected to api.redwood.dev
> GET /v1/items?foo=1&foo=1 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.dev
< HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently
< Location: https://internal.svc/v1/items?foo=1
*curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 301
```
Diana: ack. I'll start the telemetry bits.
Carlos: re: config naming: prefer `preserve_original_host` over `upstream_host` — clearer intent.
Ben: agree. I'll include that in the spec.
Alice: thanks team :thumbsup:
